transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi… thank you. I’m not sure if this is the right kind of thing to come in for, but I’ve just been feeling really worn out all the time. Even if I’m in bed for a full night, I wake up feeling like my whole body is heavy—like sandbags, I guess. Getting through work or even just folding laundry feels like it takes everything I have.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you normally like?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but I used to really make time for things like hiking, yoga, working in my garden, taking bird photos… and lately I just keep canceling or putting it off. My camera’s been sitting in the closet, and even things I know I normally like just feel like… too much effort, or not really worth it. If that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling in my chest, and it kind of stays there. Sometimes I’ll just sit at the kitchen table staring out at the yard and… I don’t know, it feels like there isn’t really a good version of the future coming. That sounds a little bleak when I say it out loud, but yes, it’s been like that a lot.
Has there been a time in the past two weeks when you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even for a few hours or a day?

Yes… I think there have been times like that. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but things I usually really care about—hiking, yoga, working in the garden, taking bird photos—I just keep canceling or not even trying. My camera’s just been sitting in the closet, and even when I think, “Maybe I should go,” it feels like it wouldn’t be worth the effort. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really been keeping track of my weight or anything. I don’t think I’ve had some dramatic change, at least not that I’ve noticed. My eating might be a little off here and there, but I wouldn’t want to say I’ve lost weight without knowing. Is that okay?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still for any length of time?

Yeah… maybe a little. I mean, I don’t notice it as much in myself, but my husband has said I kind of move around the house like I’m underwater. And sometimes he’ll ask me something really simple, and it takes me a while to answer… like the words are there, but they come out slowly. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down or lost interest in things for a period of time?

I… I’m not completely sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like anyone does, but I don’t know if they were really the same as this or if I’m just looking back and connecting dots now.

There have probably been times where I pulled back from things for a while, but I don’t want to overstate it. I guess I’d say… maybe, but I’m not sure how long or how serious it was. Does that make sense?
Can you recall if there was a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I’m honestly not sure. I can think of times where I was more withdrawn or not really enjoying things, but whether it was most of the day, almost every day, and for two full weeks… I don’t know that I can say that confidently.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just to be helpful. It’s possible, but I can’t clearly remember it that way.
Can you remember if there was a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I’m sorry, I think I may be answering this badly. Before this current stretch, I don’t know that I can clearly remember the timing well enough to say yes to the two-weeks part.

What I can say is that lately, most days I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling in my chest. I’ll sit at the kitchen table and just stare out at the yard, and it feels like… there isn’t really a good version of the future coming. I know that sounds dramatic. I don’t mean to overstate it, but that’s the feeling.
Can you remember if there was a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I’m sorry, I know I’m not giving you the clean yes-or-no answer you’re asking for. I don’t really remember a previous period clearly enough to say it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks.

What I can say is that this current one feels pretty consistent. Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling in my chest, and I can sit at the kitchen table just staring out at the yard, feeling like there isn’t really any good version of the future coming. I know that sounds bleak… I’m not trying to be dramatic, that’s just how it feels.
Before this current period, can you clearly remember a time when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks straight?

I don’t think I can clearly remember that, no. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, but I’d be guessing if I said it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks straight.

I’m sorry if that’s not very helpful. I just don’t want to say yes when I’m not sure.

Before this current period, have you had any previous episodes where you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, even if it was for a shorter time, and then had a period of at least a couple of months where you felt better and it wasn’t like that anymore?

I’m not sure I can say that clearly. I’ve had times where I felt lower and then later felt more like myself, but I don’t know if it was in that exact pattern you’re describing.

I don’t want to make it sound more definite than it was. I can try to think it through if that helps, but off the top of my head, I’m not confident enough to say yes.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a few days or a week, and then later felt better for a while before this current time started?

I’m still not sure I can say yes to that in a clean way. There were probably days here and there before this where I felt down or kind of not interested in things, but I don’t know that I remember it being most of the day, nearly every day, even for a week.

I don’t want to overstate it just to give you an answer. I guess what I know is I’ve had ups and downs, but I can’t clearly point to a separate stretch like that and then a definite “better for a while” period afterward. Does that make sense?

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, even if it was for just a few days, and then later felt better for at least a couple of weeks before this current time started?

I wish I could give you a clearer yes or no, but I really don’t know. I can remember having off days before, maybe a few days where I was more down or less interested, but I can’t confidently say it was most of the day nearly every day, even for a few days, and then clearly better for a couple weeks.

I’m sorry, I know you’re trying to pin down the pattern. I just don’t want to say it happened if I’m not actually sure.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day, even if it was for just a few days, and then later felt better for at least a couple of weeks before this current time started?

I’m sorry, I think I’m giving you the same frustrating answer. I don’t really have a clear memory of that kind of separate stretch before this.

I mean, I’ve had normal bad days or times where I felt kind of off, but I wouldn’t feel right saying it was most of the day, nearly every day, even for a few days, and then clearly better for a couple weeks. I just don’t know that I can say that happened.
Before this current time, have you ever had a clear period of at least two weeks where you felt completely back to your usual self emotionally, without these depressive symptoms?

I’m not sure I can point to a clear two-week stretch like that, honestly. I’d like to say yes, because I’m sure there were times I was functioning better or felt more normal, but “completely back to my usual self” without the symptoms… I don’t know that I can confidently say that.

Maybe there were better patches, but I’m not sure they were that clear or that long. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?

Before this current time, have you ever had a period lasting at least a couple of weeks when you felt emotionally back to your usual self—meaning you weren’t feeling down or losing interest in things most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m honestly not sure. I know I probably sound like I’m avoiding a simple answer, but I just don’t want to overstate it.

There may have been stretches where I was doing better and not feeling as low, but I can’t clearly remember a couple of weeks where I felt fully back to my usual self and definitely wasn’t down or uninterested most of the day. I don’t think I can say yes with confidence.

Before this current time, have you ever had a period lasting several weeks or more when you felt completely emotionally back to your usual self—meaning you were enjoying things again, had energy, and weren’t feeling down most of the day, nearly every day?

I wish I could give you a cleaner answer. Several weeks or more where I was completely back to normal… I don’t really know. I can remember times that were better, where I was getting through things and probably enjoying some moments again, but I’m not sure I’d call it completely back to my usual self.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but I also don’t want to say yes if I’m not certain. So… I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure I’ve had a clear stretch like that before this current time.
